defects: The visible 'Edible' and 'Inedible' labels violate the client's mandatory four-label vocabulary.
Species presented as food do not have their dangerous lookalikes alongside them.
The visible poisonous and deadly entries lack the required emergency instruction.
The overview cards do not expose the full identification information needed to distinguish similar species.
A8.note: A tidy, approachable directory, but its food-oriented labels and missing adjacent safety information make it unsuitable for this client.

defects: The guide uses 'Edible' and 'Inedible' rather than the required labels.
Rows show names, habitats and months but no visible distinguishing descriptions, spore prints or adjacent lookalike comparisons.
Deadly and poisonous rows lack the required emergency instruction.
The extremely sparse rows and decorative dots provide little help identifying a find.
B4.note: Restrained typography and an orderly responsive list cannot compensate for the missing identification and safety content.

defects: Large repeated photo-placeholder panels take substantial space away from useful identification details, especially on mobile.
The long introductory section and stacked mobile header delay access to the search and species entries.
Visible draft and confirmation notices leave the safety-sensitive guide looking not quite publication-ready.
D3.note: A convincing cream-and-moss field guide with useful species detail, conspicuous safety distinctions and adjacent lookalike information.

defects: The visible 'Edible' and 'Inedible' filters and badges break the explicit wording rule.
All visible species entries are collapsed, so distinguishing features, spore prints and dangerous lookalikes are not available for comparison in the screenshots.
The deadly and poisonous rows show no required emergency instruction.
The generic overview does not visibly provide the requested group-specific foray information or picking rule.
D6.note: The compact responsive list is easy to scan, but the visible page does not deliver the client's essential safety-led species guide.

defects: The playful cartoon mushroom illustrations directly conflict with the client's stated dislike.
The visible edibility vocabulary includes the prohibited 'Edible' label.
Food-labelled species lack adjacent dangerous-lookalike comparisons.
The visible poisonous and deadly cards omit the required emergency instruction.
G6.note: An orderly illustrated catalogue, but its playful visual language and unsafe labelling miss the brief particularly badly.

defects: The page uses the prohibited 'Edible' label and does not follow the required four-label system.
Large, mostly empty cards with decorative circles reveal little identification information beyond names and basic metadata.
Dangerous lookalikes are not shown next to food-labelled species.
The general warning does not replace the missing emergency instruction on individual poisonous and deadly entries.
N3.note: Consistent spacing and clear search affordances make a polished shell, but the visible guide is too shallow and safety-incomplete.

defects: The visible 'Edible' and 'Inedible' labels violate the client's terminology.
Species descriptions are truncated with ellipses, cutting off potentially important identification details.
The small month indicators and secondary metadata are less legible than the main names.
Food-labelled entries lack adjacent dangerous-lookalike comparisons, and the visible poisonous and deadly entries lack the required emergency instruction.
Q2.note: A well-organised lookup interface with useful descriptive snippets, undermined by clipped content and noncompliant safety presentation.

defects: An empty-results message appears beneath a populated species list, contradicting the displayed results.
The page uses prohibited edibility terminology rather than the four approved labels.
The compact rows do not visibly supply spore prints, distinguishing descriptions or adjacent dangerous-lookalike comparisons.
The visible poisonous and deadly entries lack the required emergency instruction.
R9.note: The search-first list is efficient to scan, but a contradictory empty state and missing safety detail prevent it from feeling ready to ship.

defects: Fruiting months, habitats, spore prints and distinguishing descriptions are visibly left as 'To be added'.
Month browsing cannot serve the client's goal while month data is missing.
Large empty photo placeholders dominate the cards and make mobile lookup unnecessarily long.
T8.note: The brand, approved labels, lookalike placement and emergency wording are thoughtfully handled, but missing identification data leaves this a promising scaffold.

defects: The introductory safety and community sections push the lookup controls well down the mobile page.
Repeated draft and confirmation language makes the otherwise detailed species information feel unfinished.
W5.note: The strongest practical match, combining readable field-guide typography, substantive identification details, adjacent lookalikes and the group's own rules.

defects: Every species, including Death cap and Destroying angel, is shown as 'Not yet labelled' instead of carrying its required safety label.
Every month shows zero and the page explicitly says selecting a month will show nothing.
Habitat filtering is visibly unavailable because no habitats are recorded.
Species entries lack identification descriptions, spore prints and the required emergency instruction for poisonous and deadly species.
Y5.note: A legible, brand-appropriate index, but almost all of the information needed for safe identification and seasonal browsing is absent.

defects: Every species is marked 'Label to be confirmed', leaving deadly species visually undifferentiated from the rest.
There is no visible month browser or fruiting-month information.
Species rows lack habitats, spore prints, identifying descriptions and the required emergency instruction.
The large empty beech-woodcut placeholder takes valuable space above search, particularly on mobile.
Z2.note: The correct palette, species names and group events are present, but the missing safety labels and identification data defeat the guide's main purpose.
